name: Mount Kailash
description: A 6,638 meters sacred mountain in the Kailash Range near Lake Manasarovar. Considered the abode of Lord Shiva and the axis of the world in Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Bon traditions.
historicalSignificance: Pilgrimage site for over a millennium, circumambulated by devotees despite its unclimbed status.

name: Nanda Devi
description: The second-highest mountain in India at 7,816 meters. Nanda Devi is surrounded by spectacular glaciers and is considered the patron goddess of the Uttarakhand Himalayas.
historicalSignificance: Formerly climbed in 1936, the summit was closed to expeditions after 1983 due to religious sensitivity.

name: Kamet
description: The second-highest mountain in the Garhwal Himalayas at 7,756 meters. It rises dramatically above the Mana Pass and has historically been important in trade routes.
historicalSignificance: First climbed in 1931 by a British expedition, opening the door to high-altitude climbing in the region.

name: Saltoro Kangri
description: The highest peak in the Saltoro Range of the Karakoram at 7,742 meters. Located near the Siachen Glacier, it holds strategic significance.
historicalSignificance: First summited in 1960, it remains one of the least climbed major peaks due to its remote location.

name: Vindhya Range
description: An ancient mountain range running east-west across central India, forming the traditional boundary between North and South India. Rich in forests and mineral resources.
historicalSignificance: Described in ancient texts as the boundary of Aryavarta, the land of the Aryans.

name: Satpura Range
description: A range of hills in central India running east-west, forming the watershed between the Narmada and Tapti rivers. Known for its unique ecology and tribal communities.
historicalSignificance: The ancient Sanskrit name Satpura means 'seven folded', referring to its seven peaks.
